newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-CELERIC IN ASCOT GOLD CUP TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CELERIC IN ASCOT GOLD CUP TRIUMPH.

text.p: Celeric made the grade from handicapper to top class performer with an exciting victory in the Ascot Gold Cup on Thursday, the third day of the famous royal meeting.
Ridden by champion jockey Pat Eddery, Celeric, an 11-2 chance, took up the running in the final 100 metres to deny 6-1 shot Classic Cliche, winner of the Gold Cup 12 months ago.
Celeric, trained by David Morley at Newmarket, had three quarters of a length to spare over Classic Cliche, ridden by Frankie Dettori for the Godolphin team.
Third place, another length away, went to 25-1 outsider Election Day, ridden by Michael Kinane.

Fears that Celeric would not like the rain-softened ground were soon dispelled. Eddery kept the colt running sweetly at the back of the 13-strong field behind the pace-setting duo of Grey Shot and Double Trigger, the winner two years ago.
Turning into the straight, Classic Cliche struck the front and looked to be travelling like a winner, only to be collared by the superior finishing burst of Celeric.
Celeric started life as a modest handicapper whereas Classic Cliche, living up to his name, has always campaigned at the highest level and has an English St Leger to his credit.
Winning owner Christopher Spence, Morley's brother-in-law, said: "It's the most exciting moment of my life by a million miles. I'm speechless, I've just stopped crying."
Eddery said: "I just had a good horse under me. I didn't mind Frankie going on because I could feel my horse going so easily."
The big disappointments in the 4-km stamina test were the full brothers Double Trigger and Double Eclipse. Both raced prominently but were done with turning into the straight.
Another flop was 9-2 favourite Persian Punch, the mount of Ray Cochrane who was not able to get in an effective blow.

Earlier big race honours on the penultimate day of the festival meeting went to the Henry Cecil-Kieren Fallon team who took the Ribblesdale Stakes with 7-2 chance Yashmak, a facile nine length winner from Irish raider Akdariya, ridden by Johnny Murtagh.
